w: Francisco Pizarro founded this city on 18 January 1535, and for two and a half centuries it ran the Viceroyalty of Peru -- the most important Spanish city in South America. The University of San Marcos opened here in 1551 inside the Convent of Santo Domingo, earning it the nickname 'Dean University of the Americas.'
s: Where the Spanish empire in South America was run from
_facts: Founded by Francisco Pizarro on 18 January 1535
Political, religious and economic capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru
University of San Marcos founded 1551 inside Convent of Santo Domingo
UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988

w: Lima's bohemian quarter by the sea, where the city's artists, musicians, designers and photographers have long kept their studios. Its beaches draw surfers from around the world, and a marina finished in 2008 added yacht-club polish to the ravine ('barranco') the district is named for.
_facts: Bohemian/artistic centre, home to many of Peru's leading artists
Beaches popular with the worldwide surfing community
Marina completed 2008
Monumental Zone protected as cultural heritage

w: Peru's oldest and most important library, and -- like most of the country's libraries -- strictly non-circulating; nothing leaves the building. It now runs two branches at once, an old one on Abancay Avenue downtown and a modern one out in San Borja, both open to anyone who wants to read but not to borrow.
s: Peru's oldest library, where nothing ever leaves
_facts: Country's oldest and most important library
Non-circulating
Two branches: Abancay Avenue and Avenida Javier Prado

n: National Museum of Archaeology, Anthropology and History of Peru
w: Peru's oldest and largest museum, holding more than 100,000 artifacts that trace human occupation of the country -- including the carved Raimondi Stele and a scale model of Machu Picchu. It's housed in the Palacio de la Magdalena on Pueblo Libre's main square, currently mid-restoration.
_facts: Largest and oldest museum in Peru
Over 100,000 artifacts, including the Raimondi Stele
Housed in the Palacio de la Magdalena, Pueblo Libre
Under restoration as of 2023, few rooms open

w: Jose de San Martin personally renamed this district 'Pueblo Libre' -- free village -- on 10 April 1822, rewarding the patriotism its residents showed during the war of independence. It had been La Magdalena before that, and today has more parks than anywhere else in Lima.
s: Renamed 'Free Village' by San Martin himself
_facts: Formerly known as La Magdalena / Old Magdalena
Named by Jose de San Martin on 10 April 1822
Has the most parks in Lima

w: Lima's only museum dedicated purely to European art, opened in 1923 and now run by the Ministry of Culture -- a small, specific counterweight to a city whose museums mostly look inward, to Peru's own pre-Columbian and colonial past.
_facts: Only European arts museum in Lima
Opened 1923
Managed by the Peruvian Ministry of Culture

w: Housed in the old Palacio de la Exposicion since 1961, MALI's collection runs an unbroken 3,000 years from pre-Columbian ceramics to contemporary painting. Its trove of over 1,000 contemporary works mostly sits in storage, waiting on a wing that hasn't been built yet.
s: Three thousand years of Peruvian art under one roof
_facts: Housed in the Palacio de la Exposicion, inaugurated 1961
Collection spans almost 3,000 years, pre-Columbian to contemporary
Over 1,000 contemporary works mostly in storage
